comment.narrative: CDLG survey got the following results from the survey in Uva in 202220231.Perception of Service Delivery Efficiency compared to 2020The following presents the perception of respondents regarding the efficiency of service delivery in terms of time and cost compared to the year 2020.a. Time64 of respondents reported that the time of service delivery has improved by 030 minutes compared to 2020.19 of respondents reported that the time of service delivery has not changed.8 of respondents reported that the time of service delivery has improved by 3160 minutes compared to 2020.9 of respondents reported that the time of service delivery has improved by 61120 minutes compared to 2020.b. Cost48 of respondents reported that the cost of obtaining a service from the Local Authority LA has come down compared to 2020.21 of respondents reported that the cost of obtaining a service from the LA has increased compared to 2020.31 of respondents reported that the cost of obtaining a service from the LA has remained unchanged compared to 2020.2.Perception of Service Delivery Effectiveness compared to 2020Improvement in Quality of Service Delivery Meeting Needs with Less Time and Paperwork51 of the respondents expressed that the Local Authorities LAs have improved their quality of service delivery by meeting their needs with less time and paperwork. This indicates a majority of respondents acknowledging improvements in the efficiency and effectiveness of service delivery processes.Improvement in Customer Service Requirements Helpful and Supportive38 of the respondents expressed that the LAs have improved customer service requirements by being more helpful supportive and responsive. This indicates that a significant portion of respondents observed positive changes in the attitude and support provided by the LAs customer service representatives.Improvement in Administrative Functions Allocation of Appropriate Staff and Services23 of the respondents expressed that the LAs have improved their administrative functions by better allocating appropriate staff and services. This suggests that a portion of respondents perceived improvements in the organizational structure and resource allocation within the LAs.Improvements in Elected Officials Attend to Issues and Needs4 of the respondents expressed improvements in the elected officials ability to attend to issues and needs. This indicates a smaller percentage of respondents who have noticed positive changes in the responsiveness and engagement of the elected officials.

comment.narrative: CDLG survey got the following results from the survey in Uva in 202220231.Perception of Service Delivery Efficiency compared to 2020The following presents the perception of respondents regarding the efficiency of service delivery in terms of time and cost compared to the year 2020.a. Time64 of respondents reported that the time of service delivery has improved by 030 minutes compared to 2020.19 of respondents reported that the time of service delivery has not changed.8 of respondents reported that the time of service delivery has improved by 3160 minutes compared to 2020.9 of respondents reported that the time of service delivery has improved by 61120 minutes compared to 2020.b. Cost48 of respondents reported that the cost of obtaining a service from the Local Authority LA has come down compared to 2020.21 of respondents reported that the cost of obtaining a service from the LA has increased compared to 2020.31 of respondents reported that the cost of obtaining a service from the LA has remained unchanged compared to 2020.2.Perception of Service Delivery Effectiveness compared to 2020Improvement in Quality of Service Delivery Meeting Needs with Less Time and Paperwork51 of the respondents expressed that the Local Authorities LAs have improved their quality of service delivery by meeting their needs with less time and paperwork. This indicates a majority of respondents acknowledging improvements in the efficiency and effectiveness of service delivery processes.Improvement in Customer Service Requirements Helpful and Supportive38 of the respondents expressed that the LAs have improved customer service requirements by being more helpful supportive and responsive. This indicates that a significant portion of respondents observed positive changes in the attitude and support provided by the LAs customer service representatives.Improvement in Administrative Functions Allocation of Appropriate Staff and Services23 of the respondents expressed that the LAs have improved their administrative functions by better allocating appropriate staff and services. This suggests that a portion of respondents perceived improvements in the organizational structure and resource allocation within the LAs.Improvements in Elected Officials Attend to Issues and Needs4 of the respondents expressed improvements in the elected officials ability to attend to issues and needs. This indicates a smaller percentage of respondents who have noticed positive changes in the responsiveness and engagement of the elected officials.
